cards.text: The prophet Micah just painted a gorgeous future: nations beating their swords into plowshares, nobody training for war anymore (Micah 4:3). Then he turns to Jerusalem, the Daughter of Zion, and talks about RIGHT NOW. Right now she's crying out loud, and Micah asks her why: is there no king among you, has your counselor perished?

cards.question: Micah says anguish is gripping the Daughter of Zion. What does he say she's like?

cards.text: If I came to Micah upset, friend, I'd be waiting on a hug. Instead he says go ahead and WRITHE like a woman in labor, because she's about to leave the city and camp out in the open fields.

cards.question: Micah says the Daughter of Zion will leave the city, camp in the open fields and go to ___.
True or false: Micah says Babylon is where the LORD will redeem the Daughter of Zion from the hand of her enemies.

cards.text: The LORD pulled ME out of the back of a JUNK DRAWER, friend, so I am not betting against Him in Babylon. But right now, many nations have assembled against Zion, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let us feast our eyes on Zion.”

cards.question: Many nations have gathered against Zion, ready to stare her down. Who does Micah say actually gathered them there?

cards.text: The nations don't know the LORD's thoughts or understand His plan, because He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor. They came to feast their eyes on Zion, and friend, that's like strolling into my bakery to watch and finding out YOU'RE the dough.

cards.question: The nations are gathered like sheaves on the threshing floor. What does Micah tell the Daughter of Zion to do?

cards.text: And she gets the gear for the job: horns of iron and hooves of bronze to break many peoples to pieces. Iron AND bronze, friend, and I can't even win a fight with a sticky oven door.

cards.question: True or false: Micah says the Daughter of Zion will keep the wealth of those peoples for herself.

cards.text: Micah goes from iron horns back to NOW faster than I go from "I got this" to "WHO turned off my oven timer?" A siege is laid against us, he says, so mobilize your troops.

cards.question: True or false: with a siege laid against them, Micah says the judge of Israel will be struck on the cheek with a rod.

cards.text: Then the message turns to a little town, small among the clans of Judah. Out of it will come One to be ruler over Israel, which is like the tiniest bakery on the block, ONE oven and a handwritten sign, landing the ROYAL order.

cards.question: Which small town in Judah will this ruler over Israel come from?
True or false: Micah says the origins of the ruler from Bethlehem go back to the days of eternity.

cards.text: Israel will be abandoned until she who is in labor has given birth. Micah's back to that labor picture AGAIN, friend, and I respect it, because I do the same thing with chocolate chips.

cards.question: True or false: once she who is in labor gives birth, Micah says the rest of the ruler's brothers will return to the children of Israel.

cards.text: No corner office and no "per my last email" for this ruler. He will stand and shepherd His flock.

cards.question: True or false: Micah says the ruler from Bethlehem will shepherd His flock in His own strength, without the LORD.
With the ruler from Bethlehem shepherding the flock, how does Micah say His people will live?

cards.text: His greatness will reach to the ends of the earth, friend, the WHOLE map, and my whole planet is just big enough for one bakery. Then Micah names a real threat: Assyria, whose king captured Samaria (2 Kings 17:6), invading the land and trampling its citadels.

cards.question: When Assyria invades and tramples their citadels, Micah says the ruler from Bethlehem will be our ___.

cards.text: Against Assyria, Micah says, “We will raise against it seven shepherds, even eight leaders of men.” EIGHT leaders, friend, and the closest thing to leadership in my junk drawer was the dead batteries arguing over who had the most charge left!

cards.question: Micah says we will raise seven shepherds, even eight leaders of men, against Assyria. What does he say they'll do to its land?

cards.text: They'll rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod, the mighty hunter before the LORD (Genesis 10:9), with the blade drawn. So He will deliver us when Assyria invades our land and marches into our borders, and friend, I know a thing or two about being delivered, because one minute I was under a pile of takeout menus and the next I had a CLEAN apron and a whole planet!

findings.problem: Too many choices are discoveries or coin flips for informed guesses to be the majority. Stop 1 card 5 asks about redemption in Babylon right after only the destination was established; stop 1 card 11 gives no basis for deciding who gets the wealth; stop 1 card 13 introduces the struck judge only in the question; and stop 2 card 3 introduces the ruler's eternal origins only in the question. Added to the picture, destination and town discovery questions, a baker using only the earlier cards must guess on about half of the choices.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Two important positive facts are never actually taught. Stop 1 card 11 only lets the baker reject keeping the wealth; no card says Zion devotes the gain to the LORD and the wealth to the Lord of all the earth (Micah 4:13). Stop 2 card 7 only rejects shepherding in His own strength; no card says He shepherds in the strength of the LORD and in the majestic name of the LORD His God (Micah 5:4).

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: "Those peoples" has no antecedent within the question and points back to story card 10, which is no longer on screen. The question should identify them as the peoples Zion breaks to pieces or the nations gathered against her.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.
